lesson.child_mission: Written subtraction aligns places and regroups when a digit is too small: one ten becomes ten ones (and similarly across hundreds).

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Subtract 604 − 268 showing regrouping. Watch the zero carefully.

FEEDBACK
Ones: regroup through the tens/hundreds as needed → difference 336. (Working must show how zero tens are handled.)

WATCH FOR
Subtracting the smaller digit from the larger regardless of place (top/bottom swap) is a common error.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Compute six 3-digit subtractions with regrouping, including at least two with a zero in the minuend. Show regroup marks and estimate one answer first.

Write a short reflection naming one step you corrected and why.

lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Compute six 3-digit subtractions with regrouping, including at least two with a zero in the minuend. Show regroup marks and estimate one answer first. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Original demonstration: 523 − 178: ones 3<8 so regroup — tens become 1, ones 13; 13−8=5. Tens 1<7 so regroup from hundreds — hundreds 4, tens 11; 11−7=4. Hundreds 4−1=3. Difference 345.

Parent: Written model 2: Common error: Subtracting the smaller digit from the larger regardless of place (top/bottom swap) is a common error. Correction: Ones: regroup through the tens/hundreds as needed → difference 336. (Working must show how zero tens are handled.)

Parent: Likely misconception: Subtracting the smaller digit from the larger regardless of place (top/bottom swap) is a common error. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

teach_steps.explain:
Written subtraction aligns places and regroups when a digit is too small: one ten becomes ten ones (and similarly across hundreds).

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner choose methods based on place value, quantity and accurate working, rather than guessing digits by shape alone. Keep every step justified.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the places, values or distances that carry the method. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Compare your working with the feedback: did you use the same skill and show your reasoning? If a digit or place is uncertain, identify what would have to be regrouped or counted again. One deliberate, justified revision is more useful than writing a longer answer.
